title: Replying to @Aidy - NYC Theater TO CLARIFY: it might sound like I’m j...
transcript: okay yeah let's talk more about why Hadestown deserved to win the Tony for Best Book over Tootsie because not only did Tootsie win the award but everyone at the time was like agreeing with it saying like “yeah, it should beat Hadestown in this category” which just blew my mind so there's a few points I wanna touch on here firstly do I think the book for Hadestown is perfect? I think it can be a little on the nose and I do think you feel some of the strains from when they adapted it from a concept album to a traditional musical But I still think it's an incredibly impressive achievement in book writing in the sense that she took these two separate-ish Greek myths and not only combined them but then re-conceived them as this story about resistance against capitalism and industrialism etc and all of those ideas and decisions fall under the umbrella of her responsibilities as the book writer now to be fair the book for Tootsie was probably a little cleaner a little bit more neatly structured and fine-tuned from a technical standpoint I think what Anais Mitchell did was just so much more ambitious than what Tootsie did in adapting the screenplay from the film I wanna be clear about something though because normally I don't like when people equate difficulty with quality where just because something required more visible effort means that it deserves an award over something that was maybe just more more successful or effective in context so why do I think Hadestown deserved it even though I admitted that the book is maybe a bit more flawed than Tootsie's more traditionally solid writing? because it's not just that Hadestown’s book was more ambitious I think it ultimately amounted to more I do think it was more effective more effective emotionally thematically conceptually and yes even dramatically the other thing that bothered me not so much about Tootsie's book but the way people were talking about it at the time is that a lot of people were using the quality of like the jokes, the one liners in Tootsie as the main argument for why it deserve to win best book and look yeah writing jokes absolutely takes skill and craft but I don't love this idea of using it as the main metric for what it takes to write a good musical theatre book it's definitely a part of it for a comedy obviously but I think like the big picture writing the connective tissue the way all the pieces fit together to tell a coherent and engaging story whether that's comedic or dramatic I just think that all is more important and you might feel that Tootsie *did* tell a coherent and engaging story and you're certainly entitled to your opinion but that was not the argument that I was hearing at the time for why it should win It was really just a lot of “oh but the jokes are so funny” which is part of what bothered me but again I wanna end with what I think is my main argument which is that people don't appreciate what Hadestown achieved on a book level
